note.zh-TW: 課程原字為短期放貨，網站依一般用語寫成短期放款，原字收進別名；日文原型是短期貸付金。
note.en: The course writes this account with a typo; the site shows the usual wording short-term loans and keeps the original as an alias. The term comes from the Japanese short-term loans receivable.

definition.zh-TW:
公司把自己的資金借給別人、預計一年內收回的債權。

它是公司的資產，因為錢將來會回來；一般台灣公司多把這類款項列在其他應收款。
definition.en:
Money the company has lent to another party and expects to collect within a year.

It is an asset, because the cash is due to come back; most Taiwanese companies present such amounts under other receivables.

example.zh-TW: 位置：資產負債表流動資產。借出時現金減少、短期放款增加，現金流量表列在投資活動的放貸支出；收回時走相反方向。課程的速動比率把它算進速動資產。本課故事沒有用到這個科目。
example.en: Where it sits: current assets on the balance sheet. Lending reduces cash and increases this line, shown as loans advanced under investing activities in the statement of cash flows; collection reverses it. The course version of the quick ratio counts it as a quick asset. The course story does not use this account.

misconception.zh-TW: 把「放款」和「借款」弄反。短期放款是公司借錢給別人，是資產；短期借款是公司向別人借錢，是負債。兩者方向相反，不能互抵。
misconception.en: Mixing up loans receivable with borrowings. Short-term loans receivable are money the company has lent out, an asset; short-term borrowings are money the company owes, a liability. They run in opposite directions and are not netted.
